title: Terminate live PTY actors and process groups during daemon shutdown
description:
## Finding

Daemon shutdown does not explicitly close all PTY actors/process groups. Child processes can outlive the daemon, retain terminals/resources, or continue mutating worktrees after the owner has exited.

## Evidence at audited commit

`crates/thegn-host/src/daemon/service.rs:1964`, `crates/thegn-host/src/daemon/mod.rs:519`, and `crates/thegn-host/src/daemon/session.rs:436`.

## Implementation constraints

Track ownership centrally and perform bounded TERM/drain/KILL teardown without targeting unrelated or re-parented processes. Persist enough state for crash recovery diagnostics.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Graceful shutdown stops accepting work and signals every owned live PTY group.
- [ ] Children receive a bounded grace period, then verified survivors are force-killed.
- [ ] Actor tasks, pipes, recordings, and DB state close after process termination in deterministic order.
- [ ] Already-exited/reused PIDs cannot cause unrelated signals.
- [ ] Integration tests spawn children/grandchildren, initiate shutdown, and prove no owned processes or fds remain.

## Verification

Run daemon session/shutdown integration tests on Unix and platform-specific Windows job-object coverage; run `just quick`.

## Execution dependencies

* **Blocked by:** None; dependency-ready at audit baseline.

## Additional source-confirmed finding - 2026-09-11 final-spawn review

At local main `71d8a61f`, ordinary pane destruction also has a reaping/signaling TOCTOU; this is not limited to whole-daemon shutdown:

* `crates/thegn-host/src/pane.rs:204-221`: Drop reads `child_reaped` and then signals a numeric process group.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/pane_pty.rs:207-210`: the reader calls `child.wait()` (releasing the PID) before publishing `reaped = true`.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/platform/unix.rs:373-404`: GroupHandle carries a numeric PGID and calls killpg; an atomic boolean check cannot preserve OS process identity across concurrent reaping.
* `crates/thegn-host/src/daemon/session.rs:379-453`: a Kill event may win while Exit is queued; teardown then signals the stored numeric PID.

A concurrent exit/reap can invalidate the target between the boolean check and signal, potentially signaling an unrelated reused process/group. No unsafe PID-reuse runtime experiment was performed; this is established from source ordering. Existing comments claiming the check prevents reuse are stronger than the implementation.

Additional acceptance: serialize signaling with ownership/reaping or use stable platform process identity acquired before the reaper starts; cover ordinary pane Drop and simultaneous daemon Kill/Exit as well as shutdown. Deterministic tests must never target unrelated processes. Bound and verify cleanup. Avoid introducing the same pattern in THE-577 fixtures: those fixtures will instead run inside a directly owned private PID-namespace supervisor, so this production lifecycle issue is not silently declared fixed by test cleanup changes.

Dependency clarification: related to THE-577 final-spawn tests and THE-576 supervisor ownership. This evidence extends the existing PTY ownership finding rather than duplicating it; existing machine-readable blockers remain authoritative.
